card.name: Jebwa
card.profile: The jebwa (also jobwa) is a Marshallese men’s stick dance in which performers carry staffs struck together as part of the choreography, traditionally accompanied by women’s aje (hourglass drum) ensembles and vocal chants. Performed only on special occasions and requiring the permission of the iroojlaplap (paramount chief), it involves selected families; accounts cite 16 dancers in coconut-leaf skirts and garlands. Distinct from the Spanish-influenced beet line dance.
card.insight: The Met Museum notes Marshallese aje drums "formerly were used almost exclusively by women," accompanying the men’s jebwa — a reversal of typical gendered drumming.
